word_order: SVO | Subjects precede verbs and objects follow (e.g. "They called themselves the Moriori", "Arly Velasquez ... finished fifteenth").
register: journalistic/broadcast news style (newswire or spoken-broadcast summaries — concise, factual sentences, some named entities and sports results).
non_boundary_traps: there (can be locative or part of existential clause)
omitted 'that' (zero complementizer) — e.g. "made it clear ... she will"
notes_for_prompt_writer: Treat subordinators (but, although, where) and prepositional heads (of, to, in) as signs that continuation is very likely — avoid emitting a unit immediately after them. Possessive markers (’s, men's, New Zealand's) frequently attach forward to a following noun, not as a boundary. Existential 'there' and zero-complementizer patterns ("made it clear she will...") often start or embed clauses without an explicit marker, so prefer waiting for a finite verb or an explicit coordinating marker before splitting.
